reading.title: The Layers of a Forest
reading.purpose: Learn how a forest is built in layers and how each layer helps living things.
paras: A forest is a little like a building with floors. Scientists describe its layers from top to bottom. The highest layer is the canopy, where the tops of tall trees spread their branches and leaves. In a dense forest, the canopy is so full that it blocks much of the sunlight.

Below the canopy, shorter trees and bushes grow. Near the ground is the undergrowth, made of ferns, young plants, and small shrubs. Where the shrubs grow close together, they form a thicket that small animals use for shelter. In some places, roots and vines make a tangle that is hard to walk through.

Animals use every layer. An owl may nest in a hollow in an old trunk, which is an empty space inside the wood. A gnarled branch, bumpy and twisted with age, makes a good perch for a bird. On the ground, a mouse makes the dry leaves rustle as it hurries past.

The forest floor is cool and moist because the canopy shades it and holds in water. That damp ground helps fallen leaves and logs decay. Fungi and insects slowly break them down, and the nutrients go back into the soil. New plants then use those nutrients to grow.
A forest wastes very little. What falls from the top becomes food for the bottom.

qs.q: In paragraph 3, a "gnarled" branch is one that is
choices: broken off and lying on the ground
qs.why: The words right after it explain it: the branch is "bumpy and twisted with age."

qs.q: Which sentence tells what happens to fallen leaves and logs?
choices: A forest is a little like a building with floors.
On the ground, a mouse makes the dry leaves rustle as it hurries past.
Fungi and insects slowly break them down, and the nutrients go back into the soil.
In some places, roots and vines make a tangle that is hard to walk through.
qs.why: This sentence says what breaks down the leaves and logs and where the nutrients go.

ev.text: Fungi and insects slowly break them down, and the nutrients go back into the soil.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Owls and mice are the only animals that use the layers of a forest.
Forests are dark places because the canopy blocks all of the light.
Tall trees grow best when the ground below them stays dry and bare.
A forest has layers, and each layer helps plants and animals live.
qs.why: Each paragraph describes a layer or a way that living things use it, and the last paragraph says that a forest wastes very little.

qs.q: A new plant sprouts where an old log has fallen. What can you tell from the reading?
choices: The log added nutrients to the soil as it broke down.
The canopy dropped seeds that only grow on logs in the sun.
The log kept the ground dry so the plant could grow quickly.
The mouse carried the plant there from the undergrowth nearby.
qs.why: The reading says decayed leaves and logs return nutrients to the soil, and new plants use them to grow.

clues.text: Where the shrubs grow close together
which is an empty space inside the wood
